decisions.reasoning: Two findings are failing before any processing has been attempted. Finding "picture_area" shows the recorded picture is only 1080×764 inside a 1080×1920 file, offset at y=574 — the file is pillarboxed/letterboxed and must be cropped to the live picture area before framing. Finding "subject_size" shows the shoulders span 56 % of the canvas at p50 (p95 58 %), exceeding the 55 % cap defined by gate "subject_size"; the solver notes that holding size requires moving the head down to 0.514, well within the head_target_max of 0.55 and within the scale_tol of 0.25. The "fix.reframe" strategy explicitly addresses both "picture_area" and "subject_size", is cheap, has not been used yet, and the retry budget is still at 2. No other strategy addresses these two issues. All other gates either pass or carry only warnings/info (face_exposure is a warn, key_direction is info). If this fix fails to bring subject_size within the cap or cannot resolve the picture_area crop, the next step would be to inspect or, if the subject is simply too close to the camera, reshoot with guidance "subject_size" / "picture_area".

The fix.reframe has already been applied, and all pre-process findings are passing: pose_coverage is 0.997 (gate ≥ 0.6), one_subject is 0.999 (gate ≥ 0.95), subject_size p50 is 0.41 and p95 is 0.425 (gate ≤ 0.55), picture_area fills correctly, distance_steady is 1.33× (gate ≤ 1.35). The face_exposure finding is a warn (held at ×0.80, within the fgexp_clamp of [0.8, 1.25]) — a recorded-content limit, not a defect to fix. No verification has been run yet (latest_verification is null), so no gate results exist to fail. The correct next step is the first and mandatory render: process.standard is the standard strategy for a first attempt and must be run before any gate outcomes are known. With 0 reprocesses used and a retry budget of 2, budget is intact. If process.standard produces a failing separation gate, process.separation_targeted is available as a fallback; if budget is exhausted without passing, reshoot with separation guidance would be the honest exit.

The latest verification (attempt_1) failed on exactly one gate: `separation`, which measured 1.41× against the required ≥1.50× — short by 0.09×. All other seven gates passed, including `matte_extent` at 0.991, `head_spread` at 0.014, and `head_drift` at 2.3 px. The only allowed strategy that addresses the `separation` gate is `process.separation_targeted`, which applies stronger rim lighting, a bounded light-wrap (lwamt_max 0.70), and a shadow lift (shadow_lift_max 0.04) to widen the edge luma ratio — without touching the performer's pixels. The retry budget shows 0 reprocesses used against a budget of 2, so there is room to attempt this. The `process.standard` strategy was already used in attempt_1 and did not address separation, so it is not the right choice here. If `process.separation_targeted` still fails to lift the edge luma ratio to ≥1.50×, and the budget is spent, the honest exit is reshoot with guidance to avoid wearing deep red or maroon tones that blend with the stage curtain.

The latest verification (attempt_2, using process.separation_targeted) passed all 8 gates: pose_coverage at 0.997 (≥0.6), one_subject at 0.999 (≥0.95), matte_extent at 0.991 (≥0.9), separation at 1.83 (≥1.5), head_spread at 0.014 (≤0.02), head_drift at 2.3 px (≤4.0 px), frame_count at 919 (=919), and audio_md5 equal. The two remaining findings — face_exposure (warn at ×0.80) and key_direction (info) — are recorded-content limits logged as warnings, not gate failures, so they do not block delivery. Every gate is green; the rules permit deliver only after the latest verification passed, which it has. No further action is warranted.
